extracted.intended_audience: researchers, review authors, librarians, and potential Atlas editors/authors
extracted.subtask_description: Producing or commissioning concise, expert-written surveys of active research areas for a periodically published discipline section (the ISI Atlas of Science). Includes topic selection by citation-based cluster analysis and editorial/author selection and a fixed survey format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research-front identification via co-citation analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify the most-cited articles from a year’s literature, then use co-citation analysis to find papers most frequently cited together; clusters of such core papers are called research fronts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Core papers associated by co-citation are likely to share topics, results, methods, or conclusions. The results of research-front analyses form the basis for topic selection in the Atlas and create a unique picture of science by highlighting areas of activity and relationships between fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective data source and scope (ISI bibliographic database)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use ISI’s bibliographic database containing titles, authors, addresses, and citations collected from about 740,000 articles each year from over 4,800 journals (Science Citation Index, Social Sciences Citation Index, Current Contents).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These comprehensive data underpin the research-front analyses and provide the objective foundation for identifying intensively researched or emerging fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combine computer-aided analysis with expert interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Merge the objectivity and systematic coverage of co-citation (computerized) analysis with expert human interpretation to refine and present findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research-front analysis supplies objective information; the editorial advisory board and invited experts add a human element that screens, refines, and interprets the material to produce authoritative surveys.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author selection: active experts in the field
rubrics_metrics.description: Invite authors from among scientists actively involved in each subject area, identified by the research-front analyses and advisory-board screening.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The advisory board screens analytic results to pinpoint high-impact fields and potential authors; authors were generally receptive and intrigued by combining systematic methods with their own knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial advisory board screening and role
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish an editorial advisory board of distinguished international experts to screen research-front results, pinpoint areas of greatest impact, and recommend potential authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The board’s human judgment enhances and refines the computerized analysis; members are responsible for ensuring material of greatest importance is covered and for commissioning surveys.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standardized survey content: background, current status, future prospects
rubrics_metrics.description: Each commissioned survey should systematically cover the background, current status, and future prospects of the subject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In addition to the narrative coverage, each survey must include a bibliography, a list of key researchers in the field, and a glossary to explain unfamiliar terms and abbreviations. This standard format is used to ensure consistent quality across the Atlas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Readable, authoritative, and systematic presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Surveys should be authoritative, systematic, and easily read.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each survey is the result of a long process of analysis and editorial activity, involving sophisticated use of ISI’s database; readability and authoritative interpretation by specialists are emphasized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness through periodic publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Publish surveys quarterly in each disciplinary section to provide timely access to new developments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quarterly issues (20–30 surveys each) ensure up-to-date reviews; at year’s end, compile annual hardbound volumes containing the year’s surveys and comprehensive indexes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topical structure derived from cluster analysis (subject-area divisions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Divide the Atlas by subject area (not alphabetically), with subject-area divisions corresponding to groups formed by cluster analysis and representing areas equal in size.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Though subject divisions may be questioned, they are chosen to give logical structure and reflect clusters found in citation analysis; topics covered will change as new cluster analyses are undertaken.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of cluster maps to show interrelationships
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide cluster maps—unique representations of the interrelationships between survey topics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cluster maps appear in annual compilations and help visualize connections among research fronts and survey topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coverage breadth: integrate basic and applied research within sections
rubrics_metrics.description: Sections (e.g., Pharmacology) should cover a range of related subfields including basic and applied research such as toxicology, drug development, medicinal chemistry, and clinical therapeutics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choosing sections that combine multiple related disciplines increases the Atlas’s appeal to academic, clinical, and industrial researchers and facilitates integrative surveys.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability to reveal emerging and neglected areas
rubrics_metrics.description: Use research-front analysis to provide objective information about intensively researched or emerging fields and to pinpoint unfashionable or neglected areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This objective identification of trends and neglected topics is cited as an advantage over purely subjective expert opinion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard format and consistent editorial processes
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt a standard format and a defined set of editorial processes for each section to ensure consistent quality across quarterly issues and annual volumes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Format elements include the commissioned surveys, bibliographies, key-researcher lists, glossaries, cluster maps, and year-end indexes; consistency supports varied subscriber needs (individuals, specialized libraries, large institutional subscriptions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience utility and pedagogical value
rubrics_metrics.description: Design surveys to be useful for researchers, teachers, and librarians; reference lists should be especially valuable for students.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Surveys help researchers keep current, assist teachers in background reading and recommending material to students, and allow librarians to direct patrons to current discussions across fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexible publication/subscription options for accessibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Offer both quarterly softcover issues and annual hardbound compilations, with subscription models for individuals, specialized libraries, and comprehensive charter subscriptions for large institutional libraries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This combination of formats and subscription choices increases accessibility and utility for a wide variety of subscribers and users.
